extra_checks.note: for a balanced design the REML intercept is the grand mean exactly
lme4's REMLcrit is -2 x the restricted log-likelihood; the convention is named, and any constant offset is reported rather than absorbed

explanation.stratum_convention: -2 log L_R = (N - p) log(2 pi) + sum_k [ df_k log lambda_k + SS_k / lambda_k ] + log det(X'X), the standard restricted log-likelihood (Harville 1977). The last term is an additive constant that depends on how the fixed effects are parameterised, so a REML log-likelihood is comparable only between fits that share one. X here is the full-rank indicator parameterisation named in `fixed_parameterization`. The form without that term is also reported, and any offset against a package's printed value is reported rather than absorbed (D-064).
explanation.fixed_parameterization: cell means: one indicator per whole-plot x subplot cell
explanation.verification: Stratum's restricted log-likelihood is checked against the textbook definition (Harville 1977), in exact rational linear algebra on the full covariance matrix, in tests/test_wp3_analysis.py for all three templates; and nlme's printed Oxide value agrees with Stratum to better than 1e-8 (same test file and the Oxide row above). A constant offset cannot affect any variance component, test, interval or degree of freedom. Recorded in DECISIONS.md D-070.

notes: etch_time is applied to whole wafers, so the only replication it has is the 3 wafers per level: it is tested on (3, 8) df against whole-plot error, and the denominator df count a(r - 1) = 4 x (3 - 1) = 8.

position and etch_time x position vary inside a whole plot, so every whole plot contributes its own comparison: they are tested against subplot error on a(r - 1)(b - 1) = 4 x (3 - 1) x (4 - 1) = 24 df.
That is why the two factors have different denominator degrees of freedom even though they come from the same 48 readings: they are replicated at different levels of the design.
The naive single-error analysis is reported beside the correct one and is labelled wrong for this design (brief Section 5.3).
